reviews.title: Squeal!
reviews.comment: I went from an Rx 580 to this 9060 xt 16 gb card and I'm loving this ! It was at a semi decent price, and works better than my old card. It literally is smaller than the Rx 580 and uses less power ! While newer games run like a dream, my older games like star trek armada aren't compatible with this card as its simply too new and powerful. My local llms runs alright, even at full power it runs silent . Definitely recommend for someone on a budget.
reviews.author: Mike

reviews.title: Great Product
reviews.comment:
Upgraded from GTX 1080. At $389 this is a great card. The 9060 xt is paired with an i5-14600k and 32 GB DDR4. World of Warcraft looks fantastic on a LG monitor at 5120x1440 and all settings maxed out.  Delves 100-175 fps. Flying around the Dragon Isles and War Within 55-125 fps. Outside the cities the card gives very smooth rendering. The 9060xt struggles a little bit in the cities. Valdrakken is 40-75 fps and some minor stuttering. Bogs down a little bit and minor stuttering in Dornogal, 36-80 fps.  The 16gb is very important as Dornogal uses 14 gb of the card's memory as measured with GPU-Z.
Other multimedia such as dvd, blue ray, photoshop, web surfing and such are well rendered.
Productivity, word, powerpower point, excel, scientific programs are sharp and clear.
The card at stock speeds; GPU runs 72-75C, hot spot 88-90C,  DDR6 72-74C. With memory overclocked to 2800MHz and board power setting to 9,  GPU runs 73-76C, hot spot 88-91C,  DDR6 74-76C. Overclocking and undervolting the GPU did not seem to make a difference so left at stock specs.
Drivers could use a little work to evenly distribute rendered frames. Card operates a little on the warm side.
3 month update: Stuttering in World of Warcraft was not due to the RX 9060 XT. Stuttering was due to the fact that WoW is primary a single core game and it appears that Windows does not delegate the e cores and p cores well. Solution was to disable the e-cores in the bios and, as good measure, set the affinity in the command path to the p-cores. Now core 2 is at 40-50% and the 5 other cores is at 15-25% and all stuttering is eliminated.  FPS also improved 10%. Midnight is at ~60 fps with all settings maxed at 4k, and ~50 fps raids at 4k.

reviews.title: 9060XT 16Gb is a great and powerful graphics card for $350
reviews.comment: Great card for $350. I purchased the power color reaper 9060 XT 16 GB card to play battlefield 6, with ryzen 7 7700X, 32gb ram, win11 with 4K Native highest settings for graphics. The card works great. I read many people were having driver issues and I see what they're talking about. You have to disable all of the upscaling and frame generation features in the AMD Adrenaline app. (They are all on by default) Not sure if it's just the game or the driver, but the game would crash with driver errors. the features are not necessary, The card works great only using about 11 GB. I would definitely recommend it.
